newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi fledgling stock exchange sees little trade.
newsitem.headline: Malawi fledgling stock exchange sees little trade.

text.p: Only 118,000 shares, valued at 265,500 Malawi kwacha, have traded on Malawi's stock exchange since it, the smallest in southern Africa, opened one month ago, Stockbrokers Malawi said on Friday.
Stockbrokers Malawi Chief Executive Rob Stangroom told Reuters that the share index at 112.50 points had remained unchanged since the market opened on November 11.
"The trend is that trading is not as high. People are holding on to their shares. Very few bought to re-sell at a profit," Stangroom said.

The country's biggest insurance company, National Insurance Company (NICO) listed in November with 15 million shares on offer, the first listing since the government began to privatise public enterprises more than a year ago.
"The NICO offer was relatively a small offer" Stangroom said.
Stangroom said prospects for 1997 looked bright with five companies expecting to list.
"By end of 1997, we are expecting five companies to list. We are hoping sugar companies will also list," he said.
Malawi's share market value with only one listed company is 225 million Malawi kwacha ($14.7 million).
